content: Sodium monofluorophosphate is an over-the-counter dental preparation approved by the FDA for the treatment of cavities. Common adverse reactions include flatulence and abdominal bloating. WikiDoc provides educational content based on FDA package inserts, the National Library of Medicine, and practice guidelines or consensus statements. However, WikiDoc is not a professional healthcare provider and does not replace licensed healthcare providers. It does not promote the use of any medication or device inconsistent with its labeling. Most over-the-counter (OTC) products are not reviewed or approved by the FDA but may be marketed if they comply with applicable regulations and policies. The FDA has not evaluated whether this product complies. For adults, sodium monofluorophosphate is indicated to help protect against cavities. There is limited information regarding off-label guideline-supported or non-guideline-supported use in adults. Similarly, for pediatric patients, there is limited information regarding FDA-labeled use, off-label guideline-supported use, or non-guideline-supported use. Contraindications for sodium monofluorophosphate are not well-documented in the drug label. Warnings include keeping the product out of reach of children under six years of age. If more than the amount used for brushing is accidentally swallowed, medical help or contact with a Poison Control Center is advised immediately. Adverse reactions reported during clinical trials include flatulence and abdominal bloating. Postmarketing experience data is limited. Information on drug interactions is also limited. There is no FDA guidance on the use of sodium monofluorophosphate during pregnancy, labor and delivery, or in nursing mothers. Similarly, there is no guidance for its use in pediatric, geriatric, gender-specific, or racial populations, nor in patients with renal or hepatic impairment, immunocompromised patients, or females of reproductive potential and males. Sodium monofluorophosphate is administered orally. There is limited information regarding monitoring, IV compatibility, pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, nonclinical toxicology, and clinical studies in the drug label. Overdosage requires immediate medical attention or contact with a Poison Control Center. Inactive ingredients in the product include dicalcium phosphate dihydrate, water, glycerin, sodium lauryl sulfate, cellulose gum, flavor, tetrasodium pyrophosphate, and sodium saccharin. The product is marketed under the brand name Colgate Toothpaste Great Regular Flavor®. There is no established interaction between alcohol and sodium monofluorophosphate, and patients are advised to consult their doctor regarding alcohol use with this medication. For questions or comments, a toll-free number (1-800-468-6502) is provided.
